Under ADR 0013 opening a shop is adding a row to shops; the requirements file says nobody has decided who adds that row, what a shop may configure, which plan it is on, or how it leaves.
The file points back to CH-4 of multi-shop-requirements.md (each shop's own settings, changed without a deploy) and says it has no design yet.

claims.text: Scenarios: SA-1 a new shop is open and takes its first order within 10 minutes (assumed), nobody at Đơn Hàng acting; SA-2 name and brand show in the customer's app without a deploy; SA-3 a plan change applies its limits and features within minutes (assumed).

SA-4: a leaving shop gets an export of its data; its rows are deleted after a 30-day wait (assumed); copies in backups end when those backups expire. SA-5: no shop's setting change is seen by another shop.

Đơn Hàng's own database has no shops table at stage-4 (only the lab file db/tenancy/shared-schema.sql has one); docs/design/multi-shop-data-rollout.md is a plan not yet done, and its release 1 creates shops.
claims.source_hint: db/tenancy/shared-schema.sql @ stage-4 lines 1-7; docs/design/multi-shop-data-rollout.md @ stage-4 lines 3, 21

claims.text: Estimate: a few sign-ups a day (assumed 5) make opening a shop a correctness problem, not a load problem; cost grows with the number of shops (nodes, databases, platform), and each plan's price must cover its shops' share (assumed, no amounts); the split is in cost-per-shop.md.

Assumptions and confirmers: 10 minutes to first order — product owner; 30-day wait — product owner with the legal department; about 5 sign-ups a day — product owner and sales; the Shop team owns opening and plans — team lead (ADR 0025, assumed).

Ranked drivers: (1) a shop opens with nobody at Đơn Hàng acting (SA-1); (2) no shop's settings reach another shop (SA-5); (3) each plan's cost per shop is known; (4) a leaving shop's data is gone by a stated date (SA-4).
multi-shop-requirements.md assumed a few new shops a week, opened without a deploy, and a new shop opened the day its contract is signed.

Framing a sign-up form as the whole job leaves settings, plans and leaving without an answer; opening shops by hand fails SA-1; the shop's whole path as measured scenarios fits when shops sign up and leave on their own; requirements fix the measure, not the mechanism.
The busiest hour in docs/design/capacity-plan.md is about 3.3 orders per second (12,000 orders in one hour).
Derived: 500 sign-ups in 86,400 seconds is about one every three minutes (~0.006 per second), far below 3.3 orders per second, so opening stays a correctness problem.
claims.source_hint: arithmetic on docs/team/saas-platform-requirements.md @ stage-4 line 33 and docs/design/capacity-plan.md line 23

claims.text: If the legal department requires deletion everywhere within 30 days, backups included, SA-4's measure changes first and how long backups are kept becomes part of the requirement.

ADR 0013: in shared tables, restoring one shop means extracting its rows from a temporary restore. ADR 0026: a shop moves to its own database when it holds over 10% of the busiest day's orders or a contract requires restoring it alone (assumed).
Deleting rows from a database does not change backups already taken; a deleted row's copy remains until each backup holding it expires.
